title: Mandela effect: remembered death of Nelson Mandela in prison

plain: Michels explains that the "Mandela effect", where many people share the same memory of something that did not happen, is named after the many people who remember Nelson Mandela dying in prison in the 1980s, though he was released and lived for decades after. Michels tells it himself, in a talk about whether we live in a hologram, where such shared false memories are taken as a possible clue that reality itself shifts.
